title: Unbalanced act: Biased subgenome expression during canola seed development
content: Understanding how crops coordinate complex developmental programs is essential for maintaining global food security. This challenge becomes particularly difficult in polyploid crops due to the presence of multiple copies of subgenomes (Schaart et al. 2021). Canola (Brassica napus), the second most important oilseed crop globally, is an allopolyploid formed approximately 7,500 to 12,500 years ago through interspecific hybridization between Brassica rapa and Brassica oleracea (Nagaharu and Nagaharu 1935). In canola, the genomes ArAr from B. rapa and CoCo from B. oleracea combine to form its complete genome (AnAnCnCn) (Chalhoub et al. 2014). These 2 subgenomes must coordinate to regulate the different developmental stages in canola.
